Mesillat Yesharim 9:18: For where danger is common and well-known, one must guard oneself; but where the danger is not well-known, there is no need to fear.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:19: And concerning cases like this it is said (Rashi, Chullin 48b): "A doubt that we do not see, we do not presume" — a wise man has only what his eyes see. This is precisely the matter of the verse we cited above, "The prudent man sees evil and hides himself" — behold, it speaks only of hiding from evil that he actually sees, not from something that could possibly happen.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:20: And this is precisely the matter of the verse I mentioned above: "The lazy man says, There is a lion in the road, etc." The Sages, of blessed memory, expounded this matter as a kind of illustrative parable, to show how far the fear of vanity can go in holding a person back from a good deed,
Mesillat Yesharim 9:21: and they said (Devarim Rabbah 8): Solomon spoke seven statements concerning the lazy man. How so?
Mesillat Yesharim 9:22: They said to the lazy man: Behold, your teacher is in the city; go and learn Torah from him.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:23: And he answers them: I am afraid of the lion on the road.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:24: Your teacher is within the city itself,
Mesillat Yesharim 9:25: he says to them: I am afraid there may be a lion in the streets.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:26: They say to him: Behold, he is inside your own house,
Mesillat Yesharim 9:27: he says to them: If I go to him, I will find the door locked, etc. — look there for the rest.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:28: You have thus learned that it is not fear that causes a person to be lazy, but laziness that causes him to be fearful.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:29: And daily experience testifies to all these things, from what is already plain and common among the vast majority of mankind, whose way is folly to them. But one who is discerning about the matter will find the truth in its truest form, and to the understanding, knowledge comes easily.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:30: And the matter of alacrity has now been explained sufficiently, I think, to arouse the heart, and the wise man will grow wiser, and add to his learning.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:31: And you can see that alacrity properly belongs on a level after watchfulness, for in general a person will not be alacritous unless he is first watchful. For whoever does not set his heart to be watchful in his deeds and to reflect on the service and its laws — which is the trait of watchfulness, as I have written — will find it hard to clothe himself in love and longing for it and to be alacritous with yearning before his Creator,
Mesillat Yesharim 9:32: for he is still sunk in bodily desires, running the course of his habit, which distances him from all this. However, once he has already opened his eyes to see his deeds and to be watchful in them, and has reckoned the account of the commandments and the transgressions, as we have mentioned, it becomes easy for him to turn away from evil and to yearn for the good and be alacritous in it. And this is simple.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:1:
An Explanation of the Trait of Cleanliness (Nekiyut)
The trait of cleanliness is for a person to be entirely clean of every bad character trait and every sin — not only regarding that which is publicly known and revealed as sin, but also regarding that toward which the heart is enticed to rule as permissible; for when we truly investigate the matter, we find that this permissibility did not appear to him except because his heart was still somewhat afflicted by desire — for he had not become entirely purified of it — and so it drew him to be lenient with himself.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:2: But the person who has become entirely purified of this affliction, and is clean of every trace of evil that desire leaves behind it, his perception will be entirely clear and his discernment pure, and desire will not sway him toward anything; rather, whatever is a sin, even the lightest of light sins, he will recognize as evil and distance himself from it. In this vein the Sages spoke of the perfect ones who purify their deeds with great purity, so that not even the slightest trace of an evil thing remains in them (Sanhedrin 23a): "the clean-minded ones of Jerusalem."
Mesillat Yesharim 10:3: And you now see the difference between the watchful person and the clean person, even though they are close to one another in their nature: the watchful person is one who is careful in his deeds and takes care not to sin in what has already become known and publicly recognized as sin.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:4: However, he is still not fully master of himself against being drawn by natural desire, which might sway him to see permissibility in certain matters whose wrongness is not publicly known.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:5: This is because, even though he strives to subdue his inclination and to restrain his desires, he does not thereby change his nature, and cannot remove bodily desire from his heart; rather, he subdues it and follows wisdom rather than following it — but in any case, the pull of materiality does its own work, to incite and entice him.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:6: However, once a person has become greatly accustomed to this watchfulness, until he has become cleansed of a first purification from publicly known sins, and has accustomed himself to service and to alacrity in it, and love of his Creator and longing for Him grow strong within him — then the force of this habit will distance him from matters of materiality and will bind his mind to spiritual perfection, until eventually he can attain complete cleanliness — for the fire of bodily desire will already have been extinguished from his heart as divine longing grows strong within him, and then his perception will remain pure and clear, as I have written above, so that he will not be enticed and the pull of his materiality will not overtake him, and he will be cleansed in his deeds entirely.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:7: And it was over this trait that David used to rejoice within himself, saying (Psalms 26:6): "I will wash my hands in innocence, and I will go about Your altar, O Lord." For truly, only one who has become entirely cleansed of every trace of sin and iniquity is fit to behold the face of the King, the Lord. For without this, he can only be ashamed and disgraced before Him, as Ezra the Scribe said (Ezra 9:6): "O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to You, my God."
Mesillat Yesharim 10:8: And it is certainly a great labor for a person to attain the perfection of this trait, for the well-known and recognized transgressions are easy to guard against, since their evil is revealed. But this exactitude required for cleanliness is more difficult, for the appearance of permissibility covers over the sin, as I have written. This is like the matter of which our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avodah Zarah 18b): "Sins which a person treads underfoot surround him at the time of judgment."
Mesillat Yesharim 10:9: And in this vein our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 165a): "The majority sin in theft, a minority in sexual immorality, and all of them in the dust of evil speech." For because of its great subtlety, all people stumble in it without recognizing it.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:10: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Eichah Rabbati, Petichta 15) that David was watchful and cleansed himself completely of all these; and therefore he went to war with strong confidence, and would ask (Psalms 18:38): "I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they are consumed" — which Jehoshaphat, Asa, and Hezekiah did not ask, because they were not so thoroughly cleansed.
Mesillat Yesharim 10:11: This is what he himself said further in his own words (ibid. 18:21): "The Lord rewards me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He recompenses me." And he further said (ibid. 18:25): "And the Lord recompensed me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands before His eyes" — this is the very purity and cleanliness we have mentioned. And then he goes on to say (ibid. 18:30): "For by You I can run through a troop, etc.; I will pursue my enemies and overtake them." And he himself further said (ibid. 24:3-4): "Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart."
Mesillat Yesharim 10:12: And indeed it is certainly true that this trait is difficult, for man's nature is weak and his heart is easily enticed, and he permits himself things in which he can find some pretext for self-deception. And certainly whoever has attained this trait has already reached a great level, for he has stood against a mighty battle and has been victorious. Let us now proceed to explain the particulars of this trait.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:1:
The Particulars of the Trait of Cleanliness
The particulars of the trait of cleanliness are very numerous, being as numerous as all the particulars found among the 365 negative commandments. For indeed, I have already said that the matter of this trait is to be clean of every branch of transgression.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:2: However, even though the evil inclination strives to cause a person to sin in every transgression, there are some of them that nature desires more, and in which it shows him more apparent permissions; therefore these require more strengthening in order to defeat one's inclination and become cleansed of the sin. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 11b): "Theft and sexual immorality — a person's soul desires and craves them."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:3: And indeed we see that although most people are not openly thieves — that is, they do not actually put out their hand to their fellow's money to take it and put it in their own vessels — nevertheless, most of them taste the flavor of theft in their business dealings, in that they rule permissible for themselves to profit at their fellow's loss, saying, "for the purpose of gain, it is different."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:4: However, many negative commandments were stated concerning theft: "You shall not oppress," "You shall not rob," "You shall not steal," "and you shall not deal falsely, nor lie to one another," "you shall not wrong one another," "you shall not encroach upon your neighbor's boundary." All these are various legal categories within theft, encompassing many acts done in the general course of commercial dealings, and within all of them are many prohibitions.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:5: For it is not only the recognized and publicly known act of oppression and robbery that is forbidden; rather, anything that ultimately leads to it and causes it is already included in the prohibition. Concerning this our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 81a) on the verse "and has not defiled his neighbor's wife" (Ezekiel 18:6): that he did not encroach upon his fellow's trade.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:6: And Rabbi Yehuda used to forbid a shopkeeper from handing out roasted grains and nuts to children to accustom them to come to him. And the Sages permitted it only because his fellow shopkeeper could do the same (Bava Metzia 60a).
Mesillat Yesharim 11:7: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 88a): "Theft from an ordinary person is more severe than theft from the Most High," for the one committed the sin before the misappropriation, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:8: And they already exempted laborers working for an employer from the blessing of "Hamotzi" and from the concluding blessings of Birkat Hamazon. And even regarding the recitation of the Shema, they obligated them to interrupt their work only for its first paragraph (Berachot 16a). How much more so, then, is this true regarding matters of mere option, that every day-laborer is forbidden to interrupt his employer's work for them. And if he transgresses, he is a thief.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:9: Behold, Abba Chilkiyah did not even return a greeting to Torah scholars who greeted him, so as not to interrupt his fellow's work (Ta'anit 23a). And Jacob our father, peace be upon him, explained in his own words, saying (Genesis 31:40): "By day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:10: What, then, will those answer who occupy themselves with their own pleasures during work time, being idle from it, or who attend to their own personal affairs, each for his own gain?
Mesillat Yesharim 11:11: The general rule of the matter is: one who is hired by his fellow for whatever kind of work, all his hours for that day are sold to him — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzia 56b): "hiring is a sale for its day." And whatever he takes from them for his own benefit, in whatever manner, is nothing but outright theft. And even if the employer does not forgive it, it is not forgiven, for our Sages, of blessed memory, have already said (Yoma 86a): "Transgressions between a person and his fellow — the Day of Atonement does not atone for them until he appeases his fellow."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:12: Moreover, even if he performs a mitzvah during his working time, it is not counted to him as an act of righteousness, but rather it is a transgression in his hand, for a transgression cannot be a mitzvah; and Scripture says (Isaiah 61:8): "I the Lord hate robbery with a burnt-offering." And in this vein our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Kamma 94a): if a person stole a se'ah of wheat and ground it and baked it and recites a blessing over it — this is not a blessing but a blasphemy, as it is written (Psalms 10:3): "and the one who profits by robbery blesses, yet spurns the Lord."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:13: And concerning cases like this it is said (Vayikra Rabbah): "Woe to him whose defender has become his accuser." And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yerushalmi Sukkah 3) concerning a stolen lulav.
